title: Static IP Assignment and HSBC Whitelisting
description: This test verifies that the merchant's callback URL and assigned static public IP are correctly provided to HSBC for whitelisting. It ensures only the whitelisted merchant endpoint receives final transaction status callbacks, protecting against unauthorized data exfiltration or notification spoofing. Automation: HIGH — implementable by orchestrating API endpoint deployment and controlled network-level tests.
testDescription: A merchant deploying their final response notification API must statically assign their callback endpoint URL and a fixed public IP address, then provide these to HSBC for explicit whitelisting. Only this whitelisted URL/IP should receive POST requests from HSBC's UPI system, with no callback sent to any other IP/URL.
prerequisites: Merchant domain registered with HSBC, merchant API server provisioned and internet accessible, public static IP assigned to merchant callback host, HSBC admin contact available, firewall and NAT rules configured to allow inbound on port 443 for assigned static IP, no prior conflicting whitelisting present.
stepsToPerform: 1. Log in to the merchant hosting environment as an authorized admin user. 2. Deploy the Post Credit / Final Response-Notification API per HSBC integration docs at a known HTTPS endpoint (e.g. https://callback-merchant123.example.com/upicallback). 3. Assign a static public IP (e.g., 203.171.209.5) to the callback server, ensure outbound/inbound network is configured. 4. Contact HSBC integration support and provide both callback URL and static IP for whitelisting as per process. 5. Confirm from HSBC Support that whitelisting is complete, noting precise records. 6. Initiate a UPI transaction end-to-end via HSBC’s UPI API, completing payment so the callback is expected. 7. Monitor inbound connections to the merchant's callback API for receipt of the POST request from HSBC UPI backend. 8. Inspect both network firewall logs and API access logs: verify source IP matches whitelisted static IP range. 9. Attempt to rotate/change the callback server's IP to a non-whitelisted address, update the DNS only (do not inform HSBC); repeat the UPI transaction. 10. Observe no callbacks are received at the merchant endpoint unless the static IP/URL matches exactly what was whitelisted. 11. Revert configuration to original static IP.
expectedResult: 1. HSBC only sends POST callback requests to the whitelisted merchant static IP and specified URL. 2. No callbacks are received if the callback server switches to a non-whitelisted IP or URL. 3. All callback requests are observable in logs and carry correct transaction data only when whitelisting is in place. 4. Any non-whitelisted endpoint invocation fails (not called by HSBC).

prerequisites: HSBC UPI API in PROD accessible, at least one non-whitelisted public IP available (e.g., use VPN or a cloud VM with configurable exit IP), HSBC UPI merchant credentials for transaction initiation, firewall rules established for logging rejected traffic.

Attempt to register a callback endpoint accessible from this same unregistered IP by configuring merchant DNS to point to new endpoint. 4. Attempt to receive final transaction responses on a server configured ONLY for the unregistered IP. 9. Examine both HSBC and merchant logs for denied connection attempts or no callback delivery. 10. Roll back any DNS or endpoint changes.
expectedResult: 1. Request attempts from non-whitelisted public IPs (not 203.171.209.130, 203.171.222.130) are ignored or explicitly rejected by HSBC UPI API. 2. No final response/callback is delivered to endpoints on unregistered IPs. 3. Rejected connections or missing callbacks are traceable in merchant and HSBC system logs.

testDescription: Verify POST credit/final response notification is accepted and processed by the merchant backend ONLY when the incoming connection is from an HSBC proxy-server public IP in the documented range (e.g., 203.171.209.5/6/7, 203.171.222.5/6/7). title: Data Type Enforcement and Format Validation
description: This test enforces that all request and response payloads conform to the documented data types and JSON structure. It asserts that non-JSON or incorrect types/values are rejected and only compliant JSON is processed, ensuring data integrity and parsing reliability. Automation: HIGH.
testDescription: The merchant attempts to send requests (and expects responses) with type-valid and type-invalid values (e.g. numeric in string, string in numeric, non-JSON payloads) to each UPI API endpoint, ensuring that only strict JSON-formatted and data-typed requests succeed.
prerequisites: Dummy test merchant credentials for UPI API integration, API endpoints available in test/UAT, predefined set of test cases with intentionally type-mismatched values for all field types, log access for observing parsing errors.
stepsToPerform: 1. Using an API client, log in with test merchant credentials and obtain access to the HSBC UPI API. 2. Construct a valid JSON request for any UPI API, send, and validate that the response is well-formed JSON. 3. Send the same request as a plain string (not wrapped in JSON), observe the response/error. 4. For each numeric field (e.g., refNo), send as a non-numeric string, and as a number; observe response. 5. For each alphanumeric field, submit as a list/array datatype and as a boolean, observe. 6. Submit an invalid JSON (e.g., missing closing bracket), observe for parsing/reject response. 7. Swap mandatory/optional structuring within JSON (e.g., move required field one nesting down), observe response. 8. Initiate a valid request but expect and validate the response payload has the proper JSON structure and types as per API spec. 9. Log all responses, error codes, and their mapping to test cases. 10. Attempt to resend a previously failed payload in valid JSON format to confirm acceptance.
expectedResult: 1. All APIs reject non-JSON and type-invalid requests with an error (exact wording per API or parse error documented in logs). 2. Type-compliant, valid JSON request/response cycles complete successfully, with all fields presented as defined. 3. No partial/non-compliant requests are processed, parsed, or cause system error.
